The graph above shows a parabola. The $x$-coordinates of $A$ and $B$ are $-\frac{16}{5}$ and $\frac{5}{2},$ respectively.  Find the axis of symmetry of the parabola.

The axis of symmetry is $x=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
We're given that the roots of the parabola are 
 ${x}_{1}=-\frac{16}{5}$ and ${x}_{2}=\frac{5}{2}.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{16}{5}+\frac{5}{2})}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{32}{10}+\frac{25}{10})}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{7}{10})}{2} \\  & =-\frac{7}{20}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{7}{20}.$
